properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-13, after reading the SimScale account of the 1999 Mars Climate Orbiter loss (https://www.simscale.com/blog/nasa-mars-climate-orbiter-metric/): Lockheed Martin's ground software produced thruster impulse in pound-force-seconds; JPL's navigation software read the same file as newton-seconds; the Software Interface Specification said SI; nobody compared the two sides; ground models did not catch it; the board named a systems-engineering function "not robust enough"; $125M spacecraft lost. His question: how can reflow2 insert checks that a design is done in proper units?

WHAT THE DESIGN HOLDS TODAY (measured 2026-09-13): units appear in exactly ONE place — Constraint.quantity is a "unit-bearing name" by convention (mass_kg, latency_ms) and CONSTRAINS.contribution is a bare float "in the Constraint's quantity unit". The Interface contract has nine agreement axes (medium, paradigm, payload_format, payload_schema, endpoint, operations, auth, transport_security, designation) and NONE is units. The capability signature (inputs/outputs) is free strings. Verification carries no measured value at all. So the MCO defect — a unit disagreement at a seam — is not expressible, let alone detectable.

THE OPTIONS, in his words where he gave them:

A. UNITS AS A TENTH AGREEMENT AXIS ON THE INTERFACE CONTRACT, COMPARED AT THE SEAM. The provider's published boundary declares the unit of each quantity it carries; the consumer's required boundary declares what it expects; the seam-incompatibility check that already compares paradigm, payload_format, auth and transport_security across a pair compares units too. This is the exact MCO shape (two organisations, one file, one seam) and it lands on machinery that exists. CHEAP: one field plus one comparison in an existing detector. COUNTER: payload_schema is free text today, so per-field units need a small structure (field → unit), not another enum; a unit string is only comparable if both sides spell it the same way, which pulls toward a canonical unit vocabulary (see F). And `unspecified` must read as unknown, never as agreement — the standing rule from the seam requirement.

B. THE BUDGET ROLL-UP CHECKS THAT EVERY CONTRIBUTION NAMES THE SAME UNIT AS THE CONSTRAINT. Today budget_report sums bare floats and trusts that each was typed in the constraint's unit — a contribution of 6.9 (lb) against a limit of 100 (kg) rolls up silently. Make `unit` a real property on Constraint (instead of a suffix convention) and on the CONSTRAINS edge, and report any edge whose unit is absent or differs. CHEAP: a property and a comparison inside a report that already exists. COUNTER: this only catches a DECLARED disagreement; a number typed in the wrong unit with the right label looks identical to a correct one, which is precisely how MCO happened. The honest claim is "absence and disagreement are reported", not "wrong units are caught".

C. A PROJECT-LEVEL UNIT SYSTEM AS A GOVERNED RULE. The project declares "this design is SI" (or names the system per quantity kind) the way it declares any other rule it follows, chooses whether breaking it stops the build, and a detector walks every unit-bearing field (Constraint, CONSTRAINS, interface quantities, capability signatures, verification measurements) and reports (i) a quantity with NO unit and (ii) a unit outside the declared system. This is the MCO board's own finding — the SE function was not robust enough — made mechanical. MEDIUM: one rule kind, one sweep over known fields. COUNTER: a design that has declared no quantities at all reads clean, and the detector must say it had nothing to run on (the zero-that-is-not-an-all-clear rule). Also NSLS-II and most real designs are legitimately mixed (eV, Å, mm, seconds) — the rule must be per quantity kind, not one blanket system, or it nags honest designs.

D. THE CAPABILITY SIGNATURE CARRIES UNITS. `inputs`/`outputs` become typed (name, unit) pairs, so the black-box interface at the capability tier says "thrust in N" and a consuming capability whose input says "thrust in lbf" is a finding. MEDIUM. COUNTER: 0 of 170 signatures were set when the setter shipped and the graph deliberately raises no gap for a missing one; a unit check here has nothing to run on until signatures are in the habit. The three-legs rule applies — typed tool, instruction, and a detector that notices absence — and only the first leg exists.

E. A VERIFICATION RECORDS THE UNIT IT MEASURED IN, AND IT MUST MATCH THE REQUIREMENT'S. MCO's ground models "failed to detect the error" because they consumed the same mislabelled data; a check that passes in the wrong unit is worse than no check. Add measured value + unit to Verification and compare against the unit of what it verifies. COUNTER: Verification has no numeric fields today, so this is a schema move for a case that is rarer than A and B; and most of reflow2's own 254 checks are pass/fail, not measurements.

F. A UNIT VOCABULARY AS A FIRST-CLASS THING — a Quantity/Unit node type with canonical symbols and dimension, every unit-bearing field referencing it, dimensional analysis across edges. This is the "proper" answer and the over-engineered one: a units library inside a design tool, for a check that A and B deliver 80% of with two strings. Recorded so the road not taken is on the record; not recommended first.

⭐ THE READING (a finding, not a decision): A first — it is the MCO failure exactly, and the seam comparison already exists and is measured to be the only place a cross-pair property mismatch can ever be found. B second, because the budget roll-up is the one place reflow2 already ADDS numbers and does so blind. C is the governance half and should follow A and B, once there are declared units for it to check. D and E wait for the habits they depend on. F is the road not to take first.

🛑 THE HONEST LIMIT, stated so it is not oversold: reflow2 sees only what a design DECLARES. It can force the declaration to exist at a seam (absence is a finding), compare two declarations (disagreement is a finding), and roll a rule across the design (an undeclared quantity is a finding). It cannot read the units a program actually computes in — MCO's defect was in code whose spec said the right thing. What reflow2 adds is the review the MCO board said was missing: the two sides' declarations put side by side, mechanically, every time, instead of by a reviewer who did not know to look.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: A quantity that crosses a published boundary declares its unit, and the seam check compares the two sides (and 1 more)
properties.rationale: Anthony's brainstorm; recorded so the options and their counter-arguments survive the conversation. Why it is worth holding at all: the seam-incompatibility trial (2026-07-28) proved that composition plus the ordinary detectors checks connectivity, not compatibility, and that only a property-by-property comparison across a pair of interfaces can find a contract mismatch — a unit mismatch is that class of defect, and it is the one with the most famous price tag in the field. The design has the machinery (interface agreement axes, seam check, budget roll-up, governed rules) and lacks the one axis.
